summary: Digital twin engineers build and maintain live virtual replicas of factories, buildings, infrastructure and products, wiring sensor data (OPC UA, MQTT) into 3D and simulation models (OpenUSD, IFC, FMI/Modelica) so operators can monitor, predict and test changes before touching the real asset. AI helps most with data-mapping and schema work, validation planning, drift and anomaly triage, documentation, and translating twin outputs for non-technical stakeholders.

prompts.title: Sensor-to-model data mapping
prompts.task: Map raw telemetry tags onto a twin's asset model
prompts.prompt: You are a digital twin integration engineer. I am connecting a [ASSET TYPE, e.g. packaging line] to a twin built on [PLATFORM, e.g. NVIDIA Omniverse / Bentley iTwin / Siemens]. Here is a sample of raw tags from [SOURCE, e.g. OPC UA server / MQTT broker / historian]: [PASTE TAG LIST WITH UNITS AND SAMPLE VALUES]. Here is my target asset hierarchy: [PASTE HIERARCHY OR SCHEMA, e.g. ISO 23247 entities, Asset Administration Shell submodels, DTDL]. Produce a mapping table: source tag, target property, unit conversion, sampling rate, quality flags, and confidence. Flag ambiguous tags, missing units, likely duplicates, and anything I should confirm with the controls engineer before trusting the mapping.
prompts.caution: Verify every mapping against P&IDs or controls documentation; a wrong unit or tag silently corrupts all downstream analytics.

prompts.title: Model drift triage
prompts.task: Diagnose why twin predictions diverge from the physical asset
prompts.prompt: Act as a simulation and controls troubleshooting partner. My digital twin of [ASSET] uses [MODEL TYPE, e.g. physics-based FMU, ML surrogate, hybrid]. Since [DATE/EVENT], predicted [VARIABLE] diverges from measured values by [MAGNITUDE/PATTERN]. Context: [RECENT MAINTENANCE, SENSOR CHANGES, OPERATING MODE, FIRMWARE UPDATES, SEASONAL FACTORS]. Data excerpt: [PASTE RESIDUALS OR SUMMARY STATS]. Give a ranked list of hypotheses (sensor fault, calibration, real asset degradation, model assumption break, data pipeline issue such as timestamp misalignment), the specific check that would confirm or rule out each, and whether to recalibrate, retrain, or escalate as a real equipment problem.
prompts.caution: Do not 'recalibrate away' a divergence before ruling out genuine equipment degradation; that is exactly what the twin is meant to catch.

prompts.title: Verification and validation plan
prompts.task: Draft a V&V plan to establish twin credibility for a decision
prompts.prompt: You are a model credibility specialist familiar with ASME V&V 10/V&V 40-style risk-informed credibility frameworks and the Digital Twin Consortium's guidance. Draft a verification and validation plan for a twin of [ASSET/PROCESS] that will be used to [DECISION, e.g. set maintenance intervals, approve throughput changes]. Inputs: model type [TYPE], available validation data [DATA], decision consequence if wrong [CONSEQUENCE]. Output: context of use statement, credibility goals scaled to risk, code verification steps, validation experiments and acceptance criteria, uncertainty quantification approach, and revalidation triggers. Note where standards for operational twins are still unsettled and where my organization must set its own thresholds.
prompts.caution: A V&V plan supports but does not replace sign-off by the accountable engineer for safety- or quality-critical decisions.

prompts.title: Executive what-if briefing
prompts.task: Turn a scenario simulation into a decision memo for non-engineers
prompts.prompt: You are helping a digital twin engineer brief [AUDIENCE, e.g. plant director, city council, facilities VP]. I ran these scenarios in the twin: [SCENARIOS AND KEY RESULTS, e.g. throughput, energy use, downtime, cost]. Model assumptions and limits: [ASSUMPTIONS, VALIDATION STATUS, UNCERTAINTY RANGES]. Write a one-page memo: the decision being informed, results as ranges not single numbers, what the twin can and cannot tell us, key assumptions in plain language, a recommendation with confidence level, and what data would change it. Avoid jargon such as FMU or co-simulation unless defined. End with three questions the audience is likely to ask, with honest answers.
prompts.caution: Keep uncertainty visible; polished 3D visuals often make stakeholders over-trust twin outputs.

prompts.title: Twin cybersecurity and access review
prompts.task: Assess security risks of connecting a twin to operational systems
prompts.prompt: Act as an OT security reviewer familiar with IEC 62443 and NIST SP 800-82. My digital twin architecture: [DESCRIBE DATA FLOWS, e.g. PLCs -> edge gateway -> cloud historian -> twin platform; any write-back or control paths; remote access; third-party vendors]. Identify the zones and conduits, the highest-risk paths (especially any twin-to-control write-back), and data exposure concerns such as detailed facility geometry or occupancy data. Output a risk table (threat, affected asset, likelihood, impact, mitigation) and a short list of questions for our OT security team. Flag anything that should be reviewed by a qualified security professional before go-live.
prompts.caution: Read-only twins are far lower risk; any closed-loop control from the twin needs formal safety and security review, not just this checklist.

prompts.title: BIM-to-operations twin handover
prompts.task: Plan converting construction BIM into an operational building twin
prompts.prompt: You are a building digital twin consultant. A [BUILDING TYPE] is being handed over from construction with deliverables in [FORMATS, e.g. IFC 4 per ISO 16739, Revit, COBie spreadsheets] under an ISO 19650 information management process. We want an operational twin linked to [SYSTEMS, e.g. BMS via BACnet, CMMS, occupancy sensors]. Produce a phased plan: data quality checks on the handover model, required asset attributes for operations, semantic tagging approach (e.g. Brick Schema, Project Haystack), integration steps, ownership and update responsibilities, and a list of common handover gaps to chase with the contractor now. Note where options are competing rather than settled standards.
prompts.caution: Occupancy and space-usage data may be personal data under GDPR or similar laws; involve privacy counsel before linking it to identifiable people.

prompts.title: Twin documentation and model card
prompts.task: Write maintainable documentation for a deployed twin
prompts.prompt: You are a technical writer for an engineering team. Create documentation for our digital twin of [ASSET] from these notes: [PASTE ARCHITECTURE NOTES, DATA SOURCES, MODELS, UPDATE FREQUENCIES, KNOWN LIMITATIONS, OWNERS]. Structure: purpose and approved uses; out-of-scope uses; data lineage diagram described in text; model inventory with version, fidelity level, and validation status; refresh and recalibration schedule; known failure modes and their symptoms; runbook for common alerts; contacts and escalation. Write it so a new engineer could take over in a week. Mark anything my notes leave unclear as [TO CONFIRM] rather than guessing.

prompts.title: Upskilling roadmap
prompts.task: Build a learning plan to fill gaps across the twin stack
prompts.prompt: You are a mentor for engineers moving into digital twin work. My background: [BACKGROUND, e.g. 3D artist / controls engineer / data scientist / BIM coordinator]. Target role: digital twin engineer for [INDUSTRY]. I can spend [HOURS] per week for [WEEKS]. Build a week-by-week plan covering my weakest areas among: industrial data protocols (OPC UA, MQTT), 3D scene formats (OpenUSD, glTF, IFC), simulation (Modelica/FMI, discrete-event), time-series data engineering, ML surrogates, and standards (ISO 23247, ISO/IEC 30173). Each week: concepts, one hands-on mini-project using free or trial tools, and a self-check question. End with a portfolio project idea that demonstrates an end-to-end twin.
prompts.caution: Tool licensing and free tiers change often; check current terms before committing to a platform.
